title: Premium Rating Rule — Manufactured Home Insurance
content:
The annual premium of a Manufactured Home Insurance policy is fixed by one rating rule, applied when a policy is quoted, when it is renewed and when an endorsement changes it.

## The rule

The annual premium is the dwelling limit divided by 1,000, multiplied by the policy form's base rate per $1,000 of dwelling coverage, adjusted by the percentage of the home's age band, then reduced by the total of the applicable discounts, and rounded to the nearest whole dollar. Each form uses its own base rate and its own maximum total discount.

Stated as the order of operations on one amount:

1. the dwelling limit divided by 1,000, multiplied by the form's base rate, gives the base premium;
2. the base premium is raised by the age-band surcharge or lowered by the age-band credit, the percentage acting on the base premium;
3. that age-rated amount is lowered by the total discount percentage, which acts on the age-rated amount;
4. only the final amount is rounded, to the nearest whole dollar; the amounts before it are not rounded.

**Discounts.** Discounts add together and their total never exceeds the form's maximum total discount; a discount not earned is not applicable rather than zero-rated. The total discount is applied once, as a single percentage, never discount by discount.

**Renewal.** A renewal is re-rated on the renewal date with the home's then-current age band and claims history.

## Worked examples (hypothetical inputs)

| Input | Example A | Example B |
|---|---|---|
| Dwelling limit | $80,000 | $80,000 |
| Base rate per $1,000 | $9.00 | $9.00 |
| Age band adjustment | 10% surcharge | 8% credit |
| Total discount | 15% | 15% |
| Base premium (80 multiplied by $9.00) | $720.00 | $720.00 |
| After age band | $792.00 | $662.40 |
| After total discount | $673.20 | $563.04 |
| Annual premium, nearest whole dollar | $673 | $563 |

## Named-storm deductible

Windstorm and hurricane losses at the Florida communities carry the named-storm deductible listed for the community, as a percentage of the dwelling limit, in place of the all-other-perils deductible; elsewhere the all-other-perils deductible applies to every peril.

| Community | Named-storm deductible |
|---|---|
| Willow Bend Estates (Lakeland, Florida) | 2.0% of the dwelling limit |
| Palmetto Shores (Fort Myers, Florida) | 2.0% of the dwelling limit |
| Saguaro Vista | Not applicable |
| Bluebonnet Ridge | Not applicable |
| Cedar Hollow | Not applicable |
| Conestoga Meadows | Not applicable |

*Illustration (hypothetical limit).* On a home at Palmetto Shores insured for a dwelling limit of $80,000, a windstorm loss carries a named-storm deductible of 2.0% of $80,000, that is $1,600, instead of the chosen all-other-perils deductible. The same windstorm loss on a home at Cedar Hollow carries the all-other-perils deductible.
